solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Destructive insect found in silo, customarily

indicators.note: says the letters sit inside the run of words silo, customarily, spanning the comma

explanation.surface: A farmer discovers a pest that habitually turns up in the grain store.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect is a grasshopper species famed for swarming and stripping crops bare.

clue.text: Something written in Greek requirement for moussaka: nearly 24 hours

parts.note: the Greek dish is traditionally made with minced lamb

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is left off

explanation.surface: A Greek recipe card lists what moussaka needs and that it takes almost a day.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet, so a character written in Greek.

clue.text: Trick beginning to trouble friend in French country introducing foreign matter

indicators.note: takes only the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A deception starts to unsettle an ally in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun for the act of polluting something by letting impurities in.

clue.text: Conspicuous foreigner in street

indicators.note: puts the outsider inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: an alien is someone from another country

explanation.surface: An outsider stands out walking down the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym meaning prominent or most noticeable.

clue.text: Goods offloaded from planes in the morning

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks times before noon

explanation.surface: Cargo is unloaded from aircraft early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime term for cargo thrown overboard to lighten a ship, which then floats or washes ashore.

clue.text: Facilitate Left's support for arts?

parts.note: L for left, the possessive just linking it to what follows

explanation.surface: A question of whether easing the left wing helps fund the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support for arts' reads as funding but is a literal stand that holds a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's stand holds the canvas, a physical prop for the visual arts.

clue.text: I'm just like another persona that rudely expresses hostility?

parts.note: spitting is a crude show of contempt
an image is the public face one presents

explanation.surface: A lookalike describes a double whose public persona is spitting with rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for an exact double; the phrase is a self-description of a perfect likeness.

clue.text: When texting, you are received by friend that's grown-up

indicators.note: the shorthand goes inside the word for pal

parts.note: in text-message shorthand 'you are' is written as U and R

explanation.surface: A text message tells a pal that he is adult now.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym meaning fully developed, adult.

clue.text: Evil emperor ruled and engaged socially with others

parts.note: Ming the Merciless, the tyrant emperor in Flash Gordon
led, as in governed or commanded

explanation.surface: A wicked monarch who held power also chatted with the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to circulate and chat among guests at a party.

clue.text: Aim direct shot in the opposite direction?

indicators.note: used in the sense of ruined or wrecked, so the letters of aim direct are scrambled

explanation.surface: A marksman is told to aim straight but fire the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes things at opposite ends of a diameter, hence completely opposed.

clue.text: Snappy Irish satirist

definitions.meaning: Jonathan, the Dublin author of Gulliver's Travels and A Modest Proposal

explanation.definitionFit: Snappy means fast, and Jonathan of that surname was the great Irish satirist of the 1700s.

clue.text: Partner to duck Elizabethan sailor

definitions.meaning: the male of the bird, mate to the female duck
Sir Francis, the navigator who circled the globe under Elizabeth I

explanation.definitionFit: A male duck is the female's mate, and Sir Francis with that surname was Queen Elizabeth I's great seaman.

clue.text: Everyone gawps endlessly, including only top performers

indicators.note: says the final letter of the synonym is cut off

parts.note: to gawp is to stare open-mouthed; with everyone as subject the verb is stare

explanation.surface: An audience goggles at a lineup made up entirely of celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for a team, cast or match made up wholly of leading names.

clue.text: Generally at sea

definitions.meaning: on the whole, for the most part
the main is an old word for the open ocean, so on it

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for mostly or on the whole; read literally it puts you on the main, the open ocean.

clue.text: Pacify a gorilla, say, eating small vegetables

indicators.note: the primate takes the vegetables inside itself

parts.note: a gorilla is an example of an ape

explanation.surface: Calming a gorilla by feeding it small vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym for placate, calm someone by giving way to them.

clue.text: Caught husband with excess flesh

parts.note: C, the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A man caught with a husband who has piled on the pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective meaning plump or overweight.

clue.text: Run like water, run in vapour

indicators.note: puts the abbreviation inside the word for water vapour

parts.note: R, the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Water flows and then rises as vapour.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to flow freely in a current, the way water does.

clue.text: I keep everything: retaining nothing is more difficult

indicators.note: the comparative word holds the zero within it

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps everything finds that letting go of nothing gets tougher.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a first-person self-description: the person who says 'I keep everything' is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stockpiles and never throws anything away could say this of themselves.

clue.text: Avoid duke incarcerated by Venetian magistrate

indicators.note: the abbreviation is locked inside the magistrate's title

parts.note: the doge was the elected chief magistrate of Venice

explanation.surface: A duke escapes being jailed by the ruler of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym for evade, sidestep something.

clue.text: Tapered end of grass surrounding home

indicators.note: the slang word for cannabis goes around the word for being at home

parts.note: slang for cannabis, also called pot

explanation.surface: A blade of grass narrows to a tip near a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks botanical but is drug slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp tip, like that of a needle or pencil, is the narrowed extremity.

clue.text: Unable to see length in tie

indicators.note: puts the abbreviation inside the word for fasten

explanation.surface: Someone sightless measures a necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for sightless, lacking vision.

clue.text: Had race fixed as a ridiculous pretence

indicators.note: a fixed race is rigged, so its letters are rearranged too

explanation.surface: A rigged horse race turned out to be a farce.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: an absurd sham or show put on to keep up appearances.

clue.text: Shake one dry over there

indicators.note: shaking jumbles the letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: An instruction to give something a shake and dry it off, perhaps a wet dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned adverb for at that distant place, within sight.

clue.text: Make good communist appear to lose head

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is dropped

explanation.surface: A good communist is made to look as though he has been beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: To make good is to compensate or make up for, as in atoning for a failure.
